results.title: Huawei marks 11 years of efforts to nurture ICT talent in Korea
results.content: Huawei said Monday it has sponsored the 2026 International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) Seoul Regional, extending its efforts to nurture information and communications technology talent in Korea to 11 straight years. The contest, held from Friday to Saturday, at KINTEX exhibition hall in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province, was participated by around 80 teams from Korea, Japan, Singapore and other Asian universities. It is a regional edition of the ICPC, one of the world’s largest university programming competitions attracting some 50,000 participants from more than 100 countries annually. results.title: Starfield Library decorates Christmas with goblin Santa, palace-inspired tree
results.content: Starfield Library, the famous library inside Coex Mall in southern Seoul, kicked off a Korean-themed holiday campaign. Its centerpiece is a character inspired by a dokkaebi, a mythical Korean goblin, who transforms into Santa Claus. Mall operator Shinsegae Property said its “Read the Library” campaign runs through Jan. 31, 2027, under the theme “Dokkaebi Santa and Christmas.” A dokkaebi is a mischievous goblin from Korean folklore. At the center of the campaign is “Five More Minutes of Christmas,” a short fantasy story written for it by Lee Miye, author of the bestselling novel “The Dallergut Dream Department Store.” In the story, a goblin hears a child wish that Christmas could last five more minutes. results.title: Korea draws 1,500 Malaysian company-sponsored tourists with halal-friendly travel push
results.content: Korea has attracted 1,500 employees and sales members of Malaysian wellness company BE International for a corporate reward trip, beating out competing destinations by highlighting its Muslim-friendly travel infrastructure and Korean cultural programs. The Korea Tourism Organization said Monday that participants are visiting in eight groups of about 200 each from Nov. 13 to 24, marking the company’s third incentive trip to Korea after previous visits in 2018 and 2023. BE International, a Malaysian direct-selling company specializing in health and wellness products, organizes overseas incentive trips for between 1,000 and 2,000 people annually. The tourism organization began targeting the company for a return visit after identifying it as a priority prospect at Korea Travel Mart in Kuala Lumpur in January 2025. results.title: Korea's Lee, Japan's Takaichi to hold summit on sidelines of ASEAN gathering
results.content: Korean President Lee Jae Myung will hold a bilateral meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on the sidelines of this week's Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit, Lee's spokesperson said Monday. The two leaders are scheduled to hold talks Tuesday to discuss bilateral relations, as well as regional and international security issues, according to presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan. The meeting comes as Lee and Takaichi are set to attend this year's ASEAN summit in Manila. The upcoming meeting will mark their fourth bilateral summit since the Japanese prime minister took office in October last year. Since their first summit on the sidelines of the APEC summit in South Korea's southeastern city of Gyeongju later that month, Lee and Takaichi have pursued "shuttle diplomacy," exchanging visits to each other's country. results.title: Korea flags 571 illegal online posts pitching 'study drugs' ahead of college exam
results.content: Korea’s drug safety agency has flagged 571 online posts illegally selling or promoting prescription drugs under misleading labels such as “study-enhancing drugs” and “exam pills,” warning students and parents against buying medication from unverified sources ahead of Thursday’s national college entrance exam. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety said Monday that it had identified the posts during an inspection conducted from Oct. 26-30 and requested that relevant authorities block access to the websites and social media accounts. results.title: LS Electric wins $94 mil. order to supply power gear for US AI data center
results.content: LS Electric said Monday it has won a $93.83 million (130 billion won) order to supply power distribution equipment for a hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data center. The center is being built by a U.S. Big Tech company, and the order adds to LS Electric’s run of contracts in North America. Under the deal, the Korean power equipment maker will deliver 38-kilovolt high-voltage switchgear and low-voltage switchgear in stages. Switchgear takes in electricity, distributes it among circuits and cuts off faulty lines, which makes it a core part of a data center’s power network. Hyperscale data centers are very large facilities that technology companies run to handle cloud and AI workloads. The company did not name the client. results.content: More than “just a simple display of impossible happenings,” Jiwan Kim, the magician behind the one-man act The Imagine Show, promises a more theatrical experience with his upcoming performance, which brings together mentalism and Korean music. “Magic and mentalism go hand in hand, as both explore levels of deep psychology and the study of human nature,” he told The Korea Times. results.title: Seoul launches express buses from outskirts to downtown, adds Line 9 express trains
results.content: Starting Monday, commuters from Seoul’s outer neighborhoods can get to downtown business districts faster. The city began a pilot run of four express bus routes and added express train service on Subway Line 9. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said the changes carry out a public transit plan it announced last month to ease rush-hour crowding. The new express buses follow the same routes as existing trunk buses in the city’s median bus lanes, but they stop only at major stops. The city said the buses skip 45.8 percent of stops on average, which cuts travel time by about 10 percent. The four routes link bus garages on the edges of the city to central Seoul. Express 150 runs from Dobong to City Hall Station, Express 370 from Gangdong to Chungjeongno Station, Express 470 from Sangam to City Hall Station and Express 605 from Gangseo to Yeongdeungpo Station. results.title: Container shipping costs to Middle East down, to US up in October
results.content: Container shipping costs from Korea to the Middle East fell month-on-month in October, while those to the United States rose, the customs agency said Monday. The average shipping charge for a 40-foot container from Korea to the Middle East fell 4.2 percent from a month earlier to 8.63 million won ($6,460) in October, according to data from the Korea Customs Service. The figure had been rising since March before beginning to fluctuate in August. The average shipping charge for containers bound for the US west coast edged up 0.01 percent to 9.37 million won, while that for containers bound for the east coast rose 1.2 percent to 9.45 million won. Shipping costs to the European Union, meanwhile, dropped 9.2 percent to 4.54 million won. The figures include freight rates, commissions and other charges reported by local exporters, according to the agency.

results.title: Presidential envoy expresses Korea's commitment to green transformation at COP31
results.content: Korea's presidential envoy to the UN climate summit has called for joint international efforts to tackle the climate crisis and expressed the country's commitment to a green transformation, the foreign ministry said Monday. Kang Kum-sil, ambassador for global climate and environment, made the remarks in a speech at the leaders' summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Turkey on Thursday, according to the ministry. Kang stressed the need for international cooperation on climate action and outlined Korea's 2035 nationally determined contribution (NDC) and K-GX strategy, which aims to turn the country into an "electrostate" through industrial decarbonization, renewable energy expansion and power grid development. results.title: Seoul stocks open tad higher ahead of Nvidia earnings, key events
results.content: Korean shares opened slightly lower Monday as investors braced for a series of major U.S. events this week, including Anthropic's initial public offering and Nvidia Corp.'s earnings release, amid uncertainty over the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. After opening 0.28 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) turned lower, shedding 4.21 points, or 0.08 percent, to 5,286.32 as of 9:15 a.m. On Friday, the KOSPI plunged amid uncertainty over the future of the global artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure from the company. Huang has played a pivotal role in driving the current AI boom. On Wall Street, major stock indexes finished mixed on Friday. results.title: BTS wins 2 grand prizes, 4 other awards at Melon Music Awards 2026
results.content: K-pop juggernaut BTS has won six awards at the Melon Music Awards 2026 (MMA2026) in Seoul, including Artist of the Year and Album of the Year, making it the ceremony's biggest winner. BTS received Artist of the Year, Top 10 and Best Male Group on Sunday, the second day of the two-day event at Gocheok Sky Dome. The group had already won Album of the Year, Stage of the Year and Global Top 10 on the first day of the ceremony. BTS did not attend the awards show but delivered an acceptance message by video. "2026 will probably be a year we will never forget, and I think it will be the same for ARMY as well," member Suga said, referring to the name of the group's fandom. results.title: North Korea's best exploit is your org chart
results.content: Picture a quiet suburb in Texas. A dozen laptops sit on a folding table in the basement, each hum-droning on its own power strip and logged into a different U.S. company’s network. The woman who rents the house views herself as a steward-facilitator, paid by the machine to keep them online and importantly, in the right time zone. The engineers who “report” to those laptops each morning don’t actually live in the house — or the state, or even the same hemisphere. Their salaries are not paying a mortgage in Dallas. Less than two weeks ago, the hiring process turned up in the largest crypto theft on record. On Oct. 29, attackers drained roughly $6.3 billion from Binance in what the FBI attributes to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. results.content: President Lee Jae Myung departed Monday on a four-day trip to attend an Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines and an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. During the ASEAN summit beginning Monday in Manila, the South Korean president will participate in a South Korea-ASEAN summit to discuss cooperation with the region, followed by a summit with leaders of the five Mekong countries — Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. results.title: Why kimchi maker Daesang bets on movies
results.content: Korea's kimchi and traditional sauce giant Daesang is thinking outside the box to promote its products globally — turning to movies instead of conventional food marketing. The company's Eat & Travel Film Festival (ETFF), which held its sixth edition in August, is attracting growing interest from international participants and overseas consumers. results.title: Korea to expand flexible-hour bank branches ahead of shorter banking hours
results.content: Korea's financial watchdog plans to expand the number of bank branches offering extended hours and weekend services, seeking to make in-person banking more accessible as branch networks shrink and lenders prepare to push back their opening times next year, officials said Sunday. At a meeting chaired by Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) Gov. Lee Chan-jin on Friday, the financial watchdog said that it would work with the Financial Services Commission and banks to expand the days and hours these branches operate and the range of services they provide. The country's bank branch network has continued to shrink, falling to 5,466 locations at the end of September from 5,831 at the end of 2022, according to the FSS. results.title: Korean thriller writer Seo Mi-ae on crimes hiding in plain sight
results.content: SINGAPORE — When author Seo Mi-ae came home from a college hiking trip with a cut on her face, it took her family three days to notice, even though they had shared meals and lived under the same roof the whole time. The Korean thriller writer still uses that small lapse to explain how her genre works. In crime fiction, a sentence skimmed in passing or a figure lingering in the background can turn out to matter most. That idea runs through Seo’s psychological thrillers, and it is also the theme of this year’s Singapore Writers Festival (SWF), “Hidden in Plain Sight,” which opened Friday. Seo is one of the featured writers in the festival’s new Crime and Mystery Spotlight. Often called the "queen of mystery," Seo, 61, is one of the country's best-known thriller writers. results.title: TXT weathers the storm in 'Steal The Wind'
